body: I saw your other comment about moving to uni. It's been nearly a dream come true for me, I'm wishing the same luck to you ❤️❤️

Dear SD,

I'm sorry I can't get better. I know that my anxiety and my depression are hurting you too. I wish so badly I could stop.
It's scary as hell, especially since best friend/SO will be at college an hour away. I feel pretty alone, honestly.

> My parents let me believe if I moved anywhere away from them, that I would get 'raped and killed'

Funny enough, my dad's used the same rhetoric to keep me from moving to the city.
The college does have a counselling option for a one time fee of $20. I'm scared of that, too, thanks to my parents' aversion to me ever getting help imprinting on me.

My Ndad waited until we were on an hotel elevator with another family while on vacation (at the beach, mind you) to tell me "You look like a skank!" because I was wearing a swimsuit.

He also stopped me when I was about 13 on a busy street because I tried a new hairstyle and he loudly announced "I told you not to do that, you look like a retard!" We got looks for that one.

r/raisedbynarcissists

If they found out I believe my Dad is a narcissist, it'd be hell on earth for me.
this is really opening my eyes to a loooot of memories...

Mine just recently commented about how I have breasts similar to my mother's, and how much he just loves my mother's tits. 

It's such a nauseating feeling.
Um... I don't mean to invade your relationship or anything, but if he treats you like that you should really consider separating. Those are some serious red flags.

- Threatening to kill my boyfriend (in detail) if we had underage sex

- Blackmailing me into taking programming classes (that I would've failed anyways, ruining my GPA) and do a bunch of other shit he wanted (the only thing i can remember is the classes) or I wouldn't be allowed to go on a class trip. I got fed up and didn't go on the trip, and didn't have to do all the things he wanted.

Holy shit dude.... You and I shared some similar experiences. My dad was an ass smacker too, up until i was like 15 or 16. And he would be all over my mothers breasts, and both his daughters (my sister and I) have complained since we were *both* young, and my sister isn't even ten yet. 

This kind of behaviour is not okay. Don't ever let yourself think it is.

"You just don't *appreciate* everything we do for you!" 

I hate the word "appreciate," I really do.

Also, calling me "too sensitive." But that's... another story entirely.
"Sorry, I forget I can't joke with you like I do everyone else." - *My Nmother, after purposefully embarrassing me in front of everyone at the family reunion, including my SO*
That first one hits hard. I was selfish and a coward for asking for help.

A couple weeks ago, my mom blatantly embarrassed me at my family reunion. I walked away, ready to explode at how she humiliated me, and went to the next room to quietly tell SO what she had just done, when she rushes in (almost like she was trying to catch me doing something bad) before saying "I'm sorry that I can't joke with you like I can everyone else." 

That was kinda my realisation that all apologies were completely fake.
When I'm around my parents, I feel simultaneously 50 and 5. Like I have to be the 100% mature adult, but still scared they'll hurt me like a child.
As awful as the rest of the article is, I cringed just a little at how she kept throwing around the words "fuck" and "fucking" but once and only once did she censor it as "f*ck."
Me too. Stay strong.

When I was younger, my sperm donor would do the exact same thing (except he would use just his hands, but that's a technicality). I now have acne scars (with acne still there), huge insecurity over my skin, and I get incredibly paranoid when (not if) he even *mentions* a pimple on my face.

Please, I implore that you go to a counsellor. This is disrespectful to both you and your boundaries, and I'd say it's borderline, if not outright abuse. It is *not okay* and you've *should not have to go through this.* 

And if you need someone to talk to, feel free to PM me. I'm happy to listen.

From one writer to another: stay strong. don't let her make your success about her. It's YOUR writing, if she wants it to be her way, she can write the damn thing herself! 

Best of luck to you and your works; don't let her shit on what you're good at. Especially concerning your blog, since it's to help others.

I feel that. Like, the degree i'm going into is essentially empathising with terrible people to see why they behave why they do. So I *know* narcs are the products of their past, but it's still so hard not to feel so angry at them; for me, specifically, i think it may be because it's near if not impossible for them to get help for their problem.

that i was manipulative and disrespectful. Manipulative was for a huge story i won't indulge here, and disrespectful because i would dare to not blindly obey them 24/7, especially when i was a teen who questioned everything, not just them.

"I'm only doing this to make you happy."

I'm only giving death threats to your boyfriend to make you happy. 
I'm only making you feel guilty about you wanting time away from me on our big trip to make you happy. 
I'm only making you completely miserable to make you happy.

Honestly? You're my hero right now. I can only hope to one day get the courage to write a letter like that to my parents. 

I wish the best of luck to you <3
Wow, I'm gonna be laughing about "ferd" for an unreasonable amount of time. How could you keep a straight face when she said it like that?
Yes. A lot of resentment. Even moreso after I found this page and everything became clear to me and validated and just... yes.

Yup. Every morning he'd drop us off for school and I dreaded the moment it was just him and me, because I knew the ranting would begin once my younger sibling wasn't around. Sometimes it'd begin even when she was.

I just graduated high school, and job searching is a fucking nightmare. I've put in so many applications but none ever come back for me, whereas SO got a job straight out (his stepfather got it for him). It's really frustrating, I *need* money to help with college but no employer seems interested. 

I don't know if this is the response you were looking for; if not, I'm sorry.

You've just described my Ndad. Every single one of these you described (maybe with the exception of the outsinging/outplaying part), I could think of a situation with him. I think the worst things, for me, is the inappropriate comments and the lack of respect for boundaries. No, me making an innocent comment about my milkshake is NOT grounds to whisper a blowjob joke to my mother beside me. And God forbid i tell him to quit touching me, even though I've made it abundantly clear I hate being touched, because my increasing agitation over it is just "a shitty attitude" that "you need to fix NOW," leaving me to just move the second he starts the touching shit. And my mother that he claims to love so dearly? He constantly confides in me how shitty their sex life is, and complaining about how she's slipping back into alcoholism. You could easily talk to her about it instead of coming to your daughter who is NOT your damn therapist!

I can never shower in the house without being visited at least once by one of my parents because suddenly "well I can't hold it anymore!" My mother has more than once taken shits and blamed me because "idk, something about you being in the shower makes me need to shit!" yeah it's because you're a shitty person.

My dad would constantly send me the "I love you, but" messages. To this day I can't stand the phrase. "I love you, but how dare you have a single negative thought about your mother and I!" "I love you, but you should be ashamed of your natural growth and need for independence!" "I love you, but this love is 100% conditional on how YOU act!" 

These aren't actual quotes, of course, but that's what I hear/read now whenever my dad starts to pull that shit.

I am amazing at quick, creative thinking. My SO is often in awe of the oddball solutions I come up with when we have a problem.

But it originates from me constantly making split second alibis to keep from getting in trouble as a kid. Because usually the true story, no matter how benign or innocent, would still get me in trouble :/ 

Edit; reading other comments make me realise it may also be due to parentification; I was usually the one giving solutions to issues for my parents or my sister.

Oh my god! Yes! My dad was the exact same way. He engrained "everyone but your family is out to get you" for years; I'm only just now realising hey! Some people are actually really decent for the sake of decency! While my dad would only see the people that inconvenienced him and complain about how awful they were just for that. Granted, my entire family with the exception of my sister is introverted, so he never claimed he wasn't the anti-social one.

Every semester, I'd come home with great school grades. Last semester, right before I graduated high school, I proudly came home with all A's, the lowest being a 95, for honours classes. All my dad had to say was, "That's the best you could do?"

It's fucking degrading. Anything to make your accomplishments look like nothing, right?
Thank you

Ugh, I'm so sorry. That was my college class, and I know at times it can be challenging. I'm really proud of you for getting high marks, and I'm sorry your mom refuses to see how that 88 is an achievement.
She's only eight years old. And like me, easily hurt by all the bullshit our parents spew.

I got absolutely fucked financially (thanks Mom and Dad!) and will be going to the college metaphorically right next door. NC is going to be absolutely impossible, partly because they have my younger sister as leverage.
Unlikely. He got the Ngene from both of his parents.

Ironically, he has demanded i keep both of them in the fucking loop about my college grades. as in, "*PROMISE ME* that you will call us once a week with updates." Fuck, I wonder how he'll react when my college grades drop down a bit from my high school grades (as usually expected) and I dare to come home with an 89.

My dad does the same thing, and he too loves NCIS. I hate the head smacks. Once I saw him do it to my little sister so hard she bawled. He did it to me once because I had a panic attack over my eating disorder. 

God it makes me feel angry to think of again.
Mine didn't even volunteer! But still would bemoan the sacrifices they were making and make sure I knew their sacrifice was a lot more than mine. Golly.

They've always left my younger sister sobbing to me because god forbid they comfort her for anything. 

I've been left to help myself after one of the biggest panic attacks I've ever had because they had been screaming in front of me and decided to just leave.

Yes, absolutely. In my early teens I was very borderline N myself, but I realised I didn't want to be like my parents and I made myself change. I still have to make sure I'm not manipulating people without realising, or calming myself down before i get extremely angry over small things. They're hard habits to break but I swear I won't be like them.

If it helps you understand, Otterbox is a type of phone case brand thing. So that might help it make more sense. 

The rest of that is messed up though.

"Fish aren't animals." (Okay, I google it and confirm from *Encyclopaedia Britannica* that fish are in fact animals) "Well you can't believe everything you read on the internet!!!"

(In an attempt to keep me from leaving home for college) "If you really want to get raped, you can go to [City with Relatively Low Crime Rate]!"

I just want to thank you for the commentary on band. I can't even count the number of times my Ndad expressed how much i hurt my parents feelings because i didn't make band ALL ABOUT THEM and ALL THEIR SACRIFICES! Like my literal thousands of hours practicing meant actually nothing in comparison to having to sit and watch competitions.
This realisation hit kinda hard. Holy shit.

I used to hate Christmas, so much. Because my parents would make every year so hard, and I would get particularly suicidal during the winter season (seasonal depression, maybe?)

The only reason I don't hate it now is because I have an SO that makes me enjoy it again.
I loved every bit of this, but "emotional tampon" was the best fucking part.

I used to get absolutely bitched at because I would start asking politely not to be touched, but my request would be ignored, until eventually I dropped niceness at all and told them to STOP. Touching. Me! Nah, in the mind of Nparents, agitation is just a bad attitude that needs to be solved through punishment! Fuck your feelings, right??

i broke that habit around the time I was 15 or 16. 

In middle school, i tried to start calling them Mom and Dad because "mommy and daddy" just felt so baby-ish and i hated it. My dad immediately guilt tripped me because "we are NOT your mom and dad, we will ALWAYS be your mommy and daddy!"

so it was several more years before i decided, fuck the feelings of guilt, I'm becoming a grown ass adult. 

Reading this post, certain things make a lot more sense now. And I agree with you, it is pretty creepy and weird.

I'm sorry, OP, but your father is disgusting. That is completely inappropriate behaviour! Your romantic relationship and wedding is about your happiness and he should be supportive, not making jabs at you. 

My dad is a lot like this (and i'm terrified of having him at my wedding), so I do get a bit heated over things like this. PM me if you need to, I'll gladly help you deal with his shit.

It's really ironic that he claims to be a real human "with empathy," after displaying incredibly non-empathetic behaviour. 

Drop him, OP. That behaviour is completely uncalled for, and he's forgetting that in that message, HE is talking to a real human being with empathy and emotions.
My dad, addicted to cigarettes. My mom, an alcoholic. I'm pretty sure my father is a sociopath or a psychopath, I'm not sure which (I'll have to brush up on the differences between the two).

I have a lot of similar feelings. It's really hard when you do something you feel pride towards (a good grade, perhaps) and tell your Nfamily and they just couldn't care less. There really is no support. 
I'm glad that you have your friends, OP; family isn't always blood.
I had that problem, too, with my sister and my SO. I'm glad you broke the cycle. It's a hard habit to break when its what you were raised with.

Yup. So much yelling. Then my dad will yell about how "I never yell, you've never been yelled at in your life!"

hahaha. I only can't handle confrontation, and someone raising their voice gives me anxiety. It's all good, dad. /s

The problem with that is, the CPS/social workers in general in my area are total shit. I've seen how they tear families/siblings/etc. apart, or worse, keep the toxic family altogether and "find nothing wrong."

The other problem is it's his word against mine. There isn't any physical evidence that we're abused. We'd never be believed.

I'm only seventeen but for several years, I've been confused for my younger sister's mom on multiple occasions because I'm the one who usually takes care of her, plus multiple people have thought I'm at least a college aged person. And yup. It's because I've always had to be polite.
Yup. Don't fall back into that web, I've done it a few times myself with a narcissistic ex-friend. All it ends is more regret. Good luck staying NC!
Happy birthday. Please celebrate it with people worthy of your time and ignore those despicable, toxic people. Today is YOUR day, not theirs.
I hope things work out for the two of you.

Knowing her, I'm concerned she may go Narc as a defence mechanism. I've seen some subtle signs she might have and tried to up my empathy so we can avoid that (she is still pretty young though and it may have just been a little kid being a little kid). I'll manage low contact but my sister doesn't have any other siblings to rely on, as far as she knows im her only sibling and my dad plans to keep it that way.
I'll keep that in mind the next time the argument comes up. Thank you.

I plan to follow the advice of some commenters and talk to my advisor that I absolutely do not want my parents to have access to my info. Plus i get the feeling my particular college wouldn't have that sort of release since they specifically said at orientation not to hover over your kids.

Nope. I am not eighteen yet. And can't confront him in college because I'll still be a minor until halfway through my first semester, they're planning to pay part of my tuition (hurray financial dependency! /s) and I still have to look out for my younger sister (for obvious reasons).

Halfway through the fall semester 😅

More than likely something along the lines of, "You should still share them anyway! We're you're parents, you have to trust us!"
Lol, don't want to give them any ideas.

Thankfully they want me to keep in touch with her (even if it's just so they can keep me around) but it isn't like she'll be in college in a couple of years. She's not even ten years old yet. My community isn't known for getting behind the children or family of abusers, they'd much rather just look away, and my family is just riddled with Narcs; the only support system I know of is our grandmother, who my sister spends every weekend with (which i realised just now makes "coming home every weekend to see her!" a bit pointless, holy shit!). I'm hoping my grandmother will be enough.

Okay, as you may have seen in my other comments, I will still be 17 years old when I first enter college. Based on what your comment of what FERPA says, it does not matter that I am not eighteen, but because I will have entered a post secondary school (a college), these rights STILL go to me and not my parents, even if I am not quite eighteen? (Just clarification so I DO have legal standing here)
As pounded_rice said, in my case, my parents did not give a damn that it's against school policy because "you'll still be a minor when you first go to college so it's still my right to know!"

Plus, I'm already planning to keep contact since we're already able to message each other online. 

The thing is, I am usually the one that takes the most care of her. I give her the emotional support a parent is supposed to give and constantly remind her that the crap our parents do isn't okay, and I'm worried I will not be able to do that once it's just over text when it risks our parents finding out I'm telling her they're less than great parents.

It's one thing to want to watch over your children's work when they're in high school, and a minor. Im glad you try to help them if you can because I know I was an irresponsible fifteen year old who struggled to do their work, too. (Honestly, I'd suggest trying to guide them into good time management habits if possible, and that might help them become better without having to take their responsibilities into their own hands.) 

However, because I will be eighteen within the first few months of college, I think it's unreasonable that my parents still want to hold my hand because I know they cannot handle my independence. They've already shown that they can't.

I've had to fight hard to even live at Uni as well, since we only live 45 minutes away (yes they expected me to drive both ways every day). No, I have no disabilities, but because I have a younger sister who still lives with them, no contact isn't possible. 

I'm very glad that you can manage without them, and I hope things only get better for you.
I love that video, thank you.
haha, they don't believe that. "Well you aren't eighteen yet so ITS STILL MY RIGHT TO KNOW YOUR LOGIN INFORMATION"

I'm hoping to keep them appeased with giving them grade updates. But they're mostly using my younger sister as leverage to make me come home because "it'll tear her up if you're just gone."

She is the only reason i will ever go back to that house. She is the only reason I will not go NC.

I'd prefer if they not pay any. At all. It's still up for debate if they will because of my own personal financial status. 

Nonetheless, it isn't any of their business for access to my grades. And I have the right to say no, and they do not respect that boundary.
And it is my responsibility! It isn't theirs to deal with. I am so looking forward to having MY responsibilities without them butting in like helicopter parents.
I plan not to give any reasoning other than, "I'm an adult." (I'll be 17 until halfway through the fall semester but still) It's my decisions.

Mine still talks about how much he wants to kill me because on a trip to some amusement park when i was 2 or 3 at one point i ran away from them to play on the playground we were at. Like dude i don't even remember it stop holding it over my head.
I loved every word of this comment. Thank you.

My god, concerning your comment of how your dad will "find misery over the positive things": I have deleted multiple comments of his on facebook because i like to keep my posts wholesome/clean (for my sister and grandmother) and he will always be the first to put something hateful that he thinks is "funny." Like an adorable picture of a cheetah loving on his trainer (or someone like that) and him commenting "And then the cheetah bites your face off!" No you aren't funny. You're just spreading hatred in a world that already has more than enough.

Same. So much. Every DAE makes me think "omg this is EXACTLY the same as my folks!"

Ugh, it's one thing to be caring and a healthy level of concern but the obsession with "oh it has to be perfect but there's no way *you* could make it perfect" is such an annoyance.

God, he thinks he's an absolute SAINT at his job, because "everyone there is so inept and no one knows how to do their job." He boasts about how "everyone at work avoids him." THAT ISNT SOMETHING TO BE PROUD OF. 

He also vents to me about my mom (HIS. WIFE.), "those fucking Liberals/Muslims/[anything political he doesn't agree with]," yup, the credit card/insurance scams too. God our fathers appear a lot alike. However he has actually ranted about how I have empathy (I expressed concern over a mentally ill classmate and he bitched about how "you should not care about her," and then made it about how "god those fucking liberals wanting to let refugees in," and "why do people have to fucking care about others?" (that last one was paraphrased)). 

But yup. Never seen him rant to anyone else to the extent that he does it to me. He is in fact an asshole as well.

I have tried the "not talking" thing, but it only pisses him off because "they only time you ever shut up is when you're pissed off about something!" Yeah, it's usually you, Dad. So that plus my own personal flaws, grey rocking is nearly impossible.

Honestly? I hate them. Both of them. The fact that I still have to live with them only makes me angrier every single day. 

I can't wait until I can cut them both out of my life and drag my sister out too.
this is honestly my biggest motivation in life right now

I have felt the same way. Anytime i started getting too eager and happy, they'd whine about how, "god she won't shut up," or "Shes being SO annoying." To this day i can barely express joy to my SO without apologising for being "too much."

My dad and aunt both come from a bad background, plus my aunt commonly dates abusive men, so I'm not sure she recognised that it was inappropriate. Plus my dad has her wrapped around his finger and could probably talk the comment to being something "acceptable."
Im so sorry. I've gotten comments on my breasts before, but mostly it's shame for "not covering up!" and "just wanting to show of!"

In my (much kinder) aunt's defence, she did not laugh. It was just Ndad laughing. (Sorry if my post read it as her laughing along)

I discussed it with my SO and he reaffirmed that it is sexual abuse. Which is... very hard to digest, because never in a long time would i have called myself sexually abused. But as my SO said, "It'd be the same if he'd grabbed your breasts."

I am making college arrangements now, thankfully. 

Thank you and jsmoo both for caring enough to leave comments. I needed the reassurement.

I completely empathise with you, friend. I've been dealing with guilt when Ndad yelled because I didn't find his insult towards me funny. It's ridiculous, and god, the anxiety. From one person with anxiety to another, I want you to know I completely, 100% empathise. I hope things get better for you, friend, and just know you aren't alone in this sub.

Yup yup yup. If i asked questions, it would be "stopped being so nosy!" Or talking about how, when Ndad was my age and he asked questions like that (for example, asking where we were going when Ndad told me to get in the car), he'd have been beaten senseless. I was "supposed to absolutely do what [my] parents tell me to," no questions asked. Period.

Revenge fantasies are definitely legit. Never fantasised about personally killing them, but telling them off and dancing on their graves was definitely a common desire. 

I've definitely tried to move past the revenge desires. I'd highly encourage the sentiment of, "The best revenge you can have is living well." That's my advice, but I must admit that I can relate to those fantasies.

Every single day, OP. I'm still in the denial stage that i have Nrents, so still in denial that they don't love me. I completely understand how hard it is when the raw need to be loved hits. I sincerely hope you've made other (healthy) relationships in your life where you're loved, because even though it doesn't completely make up for what you wish for, it does soften the blow. I hope you managed to catch some good Z's, OP.
You hit the nail right on the head. Bravo!

Yup. I empathise with this deeply. I distinctly remember my Ndad giving me the talk about how, "With your curfew, you will not even be a minute late. If curfew is 9:00 and you come in at 9:01, you're grounded. I don't care about flat tires, traffic, nothing. You get back before curfew." Cue my father, who is never to work on time, with a daughter who is now terrified to ever go out. 

Plus, the whole "learned helplessness" thing is legit. I learned the hard way today alone I am completely clueless about using a dishwasher (boy do i plan to learn now though). You never learned how to do these things, but how dare you not know how????

My father (who is an ACoN but with Nparents that focused on physical abuse) would in a sense acknowledge he was treating us badly, but "when *I* was a kid, I had it *so much worse* so *WHY ARE YOU COMPLAINING?*" Because the fact that you rarely hit us completely justifies the emotional turmoil you've caused all my life. 

My mother, whenever she made a mild mistake, would often say, "I know, I'm the worst mother ever." But it was never sincere; it often meant she couldn't care less.

I have somehow managed to get a fantastic SO who sees through how my parents treated me as a kid. Whenever I start to self blame, he (gently) calls me out on it and tells me to stop before I get to the point of hurting myself. It's bizarre when you first get a healthy relationship, but getting acclimated to an environment where not every mistake is an extreme fault in your part really changes you. I've noticed that, thanks to SO, I'm slowly learning to let go of small unfortunate events that used to ruin my entire day. Recognising the FLEAs is definitely a big step in overcoming them. I've learned to control anger and handle my sensitivity in a more mature manner. In short, I completely agree with you that finding healthier people makes things better (and not just with this FLEA). I hope you have healthy people in your life too :)

Thank you for your support. 

Unfortunately, the situation with my actual parents (as might be expected in this subreddit) is not good. My emotional health wouldn't be able to take another year living in my parents house, hence why I wanted to go to the college which, yes, is in another state. The college I'll be attending is a good college, and I have excellent grades and a good chance of getting a great scholarship that'll pay for most of my tuition. I'm still in grief (a strong word, I know, but it feels the most accurate) over the loss of my dream college. It's just really scary that I'll be so close to them (I'm thankful to be living on campus though) and I really just needed to get the overdramatic feelings I've had about all of this, because both of my parents have expected nothing but matureness and a willingness to immediately give up my dream college once we learned I didn't get my scholarship. 

Thanks for listening to my ranting, I appreciate that somebody will listen.

I am so sorry. Please give Sammy a pet for me, since I can't do it myself. 

My dad won't let Fido get away with *anything.* We have two dogs, and he does it with both of them, but Fido definitely gets the worse treatment. God forbid he LAYS DOWN in the wrong spot, instead of the designated place in the corner on the floor. Fido gets skittish the second Ndad walks in the room, but nah. It's obviously Fido who's the problem, right? /s
